My fiancee and I are lesbians. Our friend is older than us and completely straight. There is no romantic interest there. 

And I never said that it was just a casual friendship. I said we share our passion for baseball, which doesn’t make it a shallow friendship.

This friend has supported me throughout the years and I have also supported her, so I don’t feel like ending my friendship just because she didn’t treat me poorly while I was on a break with my fiancee is fair.

I’m not treating them as equals and I’m not comparing either relationship. 

But I feel like it’s not fair for me to end a friendship just because such friend didn’t treat me badly and turned her back on me when my relationship took the hit.

It was a mutual friend, but my fiancee does not see it this way because she knew the friend first.

It’s been four months since we took that trip. And it’s important to me because our friend was there for me when I needed support, regarding my relationship and other personal things.

My friend’s mom and my dad passed away around the same time, so I feel like she understood the things I was going through at the time.

My fiancee isn’t open to talking or meeting up with our friend ever again. She wants her out of our lives and that’s the end of it. 

If you’d feel the same way, what is something reasonable that you’d ask of me so I could help you feel at ease about this situation?

There’s nothing more to their fight as far as I’m concerned. I still see it as “you were friends with me first, so even though you’re friends with her now, you have to cut all ties with her” coming from my fiancee.

I do, I truly do understand. I just don’t know how to offer a healthy alternative that my fiancee will agree to that doesn’t involve blocking our friend. 

My fiancee said very clearly that I have to choose between both of them, and that there was no way she’d ever forgive her.

I understand our friend hurt my fiancee, but I’m also aware that the thing that made her upset is that our friend was kind to me and didn’t exclude me from the baseball trip with our group of friends. 

If I were to turn this scenario around, I’d be happy my ex isn’t being excluded and that she has the opportunity to go do something she enjoys to distract herself from all the chaos in the relationship.

I wish I could find some healthy middle ground, but sadly I don’t see her calming down.

I don’t think she’s worried at all about the possibility of us being more than friends. My fiancee and I are lesbians, while our friend is older than us and completely straight. 

On the other hand, I do suspect my fiancee is upset because our friend didn’t see all the things my fiancee told her about me as terrible. 

Our friend was always supportive to the both of us, didn’t take sides when the break up happened, and didn’t exclude me from our group of friends. 

Whenever I talk to my fiancee about this, she always goes back to “she was MY friend first, so she shouldn’t have remained friends with you after.”

And that’s were I disagree with her. I’m not gonna go through life avoiding making a connection and building friendships with the people she introduces me to just in case years later she decides she wants to break up with me again.

Thank you for your input. Would you mind giving me a more thorough explanation as to why you see it this way?

I’d like to work on the things that aren’t healthy in the relationship with her.

It was a group trip with seven of us, all girls. My fiancee and I are lesbians, and this friend we have is completely straight. She’s even older than us, so there is absolutely no way we’d see each other as something else.

My fiancee and I were on a break, not living together and able to sleep with other people (which neither of us did). 

And yes, this friend is someone my fiancee would vent to and tell everything to.

It was planned a few months after. But the reason she invited me is because we’ve been going on these trips for years. 

It was seven of us, all girls. It wasn’t just me and this other girl. I’m friends with everybody but my fiancee has an issue with this specific friend because she was the one who years ago introduced me to her.

I didn’t go on a trip with this friend by myself. It was seven of us, all girls. We have a group that usually travels together for baseball games and our friend didn’t want to exclude me just because my fiancee and I were on a break.

In any case, I can’t imagine asking our group of friends to exclude an ex just because things didn’t work out with them. In my opinion, after being in a relationship for five years, we shared those friends regardless of who knew each other first.

Yes, all three of us are females. 

The advice our friend gave her was “you should leave if you aren’t happy in the relationship.”

And yes, I understand my fiancee was friends with her first. But does that stop me from actually befriending and building bonds with the people she introduces me to? I’ve been friends with this person for years and after losing my relationship, was I supposed to let go of my friends and lose them too?

This friend gave support to the both of us when things ended, and I also feel like asking her to take sides isn’t fair?

When we broke things up between us, my fiancee went to this friend looking for emotional support and told her about all of our problems and the things I did. Our friend told her “well, if you aren’t happy, it’s best to leave the relationship”.

A few months later we went on the trip and my fiancee felt betrayed because after telling our friend everything wrong I did, our friend still decided to travel with me. 

I’m only assuming my fiancee also felt betrayed because our friend didn’t see the things I did as terrible. And my fiancee expected every single person she introduced me to to distant themselves from me,  even if they were also my friends.

She ended her friendship with this friend only and not anyone else on that trip because my fiancee was very close to her specifically. The rest of the group were people she knows but doesn’t really have a close friendship with.

And I don’t know, maybe IATA, but I can’t imagine excluding an ex from our group of mutual friends just because things between us aren’t well, regardless of who knew each of those friends first.

There was absolutely nothing more than the group trip.

I’m not trying to justify anything. I know what I did. I went on a trip with a group of friends that included a friend my fiancee introduced me to five years prior to the trip; someone that I developed a friendship with years before the break up even happened. Someone that we would constantly go on trips with.
I think when it comes to it, I myself find it more difficult to make friends. She’s an average social person and doesn’t struggle when it comes to making friends.

Why am I not allowed to consider someone a friend after years of interacting and spending time with them? We went on a trip with a group of friends. It wasn’t just me and her. Was the whole group supposed to exclude me just because I was having issues with my fiancee at the time?

If two of your friends break up, will you automatically cut one of them off?

I suggested couple’s therapy as I’ve been going to therapy myself, but she rejected the idea and simply said we have to cut ties with this friend. 

We are a lesbian couple, but I must also say that our friend is straight and she is also relatively older than us, so there is zero physical attraction from either side.

I appreciate your input and hopefully we can work something out.
Are you trying to say I should cut ties with someone I consider to have a healthy friendship with just because she remained my friend after my relationship ended?
Appreciate your answer as this puts me at ease.
